fix/audit-cycle-33987355439, output-neutral by design and by QA (the seven-commit chain was squashed into two commits before merge): 6368e56 raises the local relink deadline, keeps an unpublished packed payload and accepts the plain 'relink' run as a first recovery source, naming the rejected condition (workflow timing, packaging and recovery admission only); e57202a demotes the per-DH-query resolver log line to DEBUG and adds progress/done lines (logging only; the cached query result is unchanged), makes the per-book claim exclusive on every relink and removes artifacts EAFP (scheduling and file handling only; each book is still linked once by the same code), starts a fresh worker before each heavy book and requeues a MemoryError'd book once (worker lifecycle only; a requeued book is recomputed identically), adds GPU telemetry, mongod ownership and fork hygiene (observability and process cleanup only), and counts link records during the existing baseline digest pass to publish relink_work.json (provenance only). No change to link computation, ambiguity policy or artifact bytes; engine_src and sefaria_patch move only because those files are hashed.

fix(pool): process ownership, cleanup and heartbeat accounting only. Pool workers retain the same work assignment and link algorithm; the change drains an old token-bound worker generation before replacement, namespaces advisory heartbeat files and extends GPU telemetry parsing. It does not change source normalization, reference resolution, ambiguity policy, link records or artifact bytes.

fix(pool): process lifecycle and cleanup attribution only. Linux observes a dead pool leader with waitid(WNOWAIT), preserving the original PID/PGID/SID identity until all same-session descendants are drained and the leader is reaped; environments, work assignment and link computation are unchanged. This cannot change normalization, resolution, ambiguity policy, link records or artifact bytes.

5bd8a33 feat(linker): pool memory governor, commit gate and progress-bounded memory retries - worker lifecycle and scheduling only. With no memory trouble the new code does nothing (process_batch, records and write_artifact unchanged; the published-book file lives outside artifacts/ and checkpoints; the packer excludes only temp names a clean tree never has). A governor abort or kill resumes the book from its committed shards through the existing checkpoint contract, and the commit gate (sys.monitoring RAISE + taint) guarantees nothing computed after any MemoryError or abort in a worker image is ever written. Reviewed by three adversarial QA passes (the last verdict: output-neutral yes). No change to normalization, resolution, ambiguity policy, link records or artifact bytes.
